judgments.reasoning_cat1: The item is a fill-in block whose options ('Retain'/'Cancel' balance of term insurance, plan, amount, date, beneficiary 'Same as original policy') are left largely unmarked and the text is fragmentary, so what was elected cannot be determined from the words. The mixed-in smoker-class options ('Change to Non-Smoker', 'Change to Select Non-Smoker') sit oddly inside a term-conversion item, creating scope uncertainty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with item 3 (change of basic amount) and the Home Office Endorsement block, an unexercised conversion option does not contradict anything operative, but the beneficiary alternatives cross-reference Form 3116 which is not before us.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple mode-election box with blank amounts; the only wording issue is the garbled cross-reference ('CMAPP Section 03') and the undefined 'ABC' mode, which are labels rather than operative ambiguities.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the premium payment mode block earlier in the form (Ann./S.A./Qua./ABC/Other), and no other provision fixes a conflicting mode.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A yes/no question with an instruction to submit 'appropriate NEW assignment forms'; 'appropriate' is loose but the sentence's operation is plain and administrative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits beside the loan block, which itself assigns all right, title and interest in the policy to Ohio National as security, so the two assignment mechanisms could be read as overlapping, though not contradictory.
judgments.clause_name: Assignment of converted or changed policy

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is a bare heading with no substantive content, and 'guaranteed purchase option' is not defined anywhere on the form, so its scope depends entirely on the underlying policy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The adjacent option/occasion list (Regular Option, Marriage, Birth or Adoption) supplies the detail, so the heading is consistent with the surrounding block.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The loan text mixes 'Cash (Amount of Check)', 'Gross (Amount of Loan)' and the statement that 'on full or gross loans, policy loan interest is deducted while loan interest is added to any net loan', and the undefined terms 'full', 'gross' and 'net' loan plus the OCR-broken interest-rate reference leave the computation genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It assigns all right, title and interest in the policy to Ohio National as sole security, which overlaps the separate assignment question and the release provision (3), but is expressly made 'subject to all terms of the policy', which harmonises it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The operative figure is incomplete — 'Change basic amount from $252000 to $___' with no new amount supplied — so the provision on its face does not state what change was made, a mechanical defect that goes to meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears directly on item 6 (change to paid-up insurance for $__) and on the ratification clause (2), which forbids any change in 'amount' unless the owner agrees in writing, so a dispute about what amount the policy carried would turn on the interplay.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Both 'type' blanks are empty and 'type' is undefined on the form, so the item states no ascertainable change.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels items 3 and 6 and the ratification clause's reference to 'plan or benefits'; nothing in the form contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard replacement question; 'intended to serve as a replacement, in whole or in part' is slightly open-textured but is a conventional and workable formulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision of the form addresses replacement, so there is nothing to conflict with.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The fragment offers 'Amount of check' against 'Gross (Amount of withdrawal including charges)' without stating which governs absent an election, and the surrounding text is lost.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors the cash/gross distinction in the loan block, and the two are consistent in structure though the charges treatment is not spelled out anywhere else.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The instruction is internally garbled — box B is described as electing 'withholding apply' where the preceding clause covers non-withholding — so the reader cannot reliably tell which box does what from this sentence alone.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The separate box A and box B election lines (provisions 14 and 16) supply the correct sense, so the instruction can be harmonised with them despite the garbling.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paid-up insurance election is run together with unrelated tax text, and its parenthetical that additional benefit provisions 'terminate according to its terms unless otherwise provided' leaves the trigger and the escape clause both indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps item 8 (cancel Supplementary Agreements) and clause 3 (release on cancellation of any part of the policy), so whether riders end automatically or only on express cancellation is a point of tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The tax-liability notice is a statutory-style warning, but as reproduced it is spliced with the paid-up insurance parenthetical and the rating item, so its sentences do not close.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the substance of the withholding instructions and box elections without contradicting them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The operative sense — future monthly insurance costs charged on the reduced or removed rating — is clear, though the sentence is contaminated by stray withholding text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other item on the form addresses rating or cost of insurance, so there is nothing to conflict with; the ratification clause's reference to 'risk class' is complementary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line election with a single definite meaning; only OCR noise affects it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the withholding instructions and the tax notice, which anticipate exactly this election.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The item is an open blank for naming 'Supplementary Agreement(s)', a term nowhere defined on the form, so its reach depends on the policy documents.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against item 6's statement that additional benefit provisions terminate according to their terms and clause 3's release language, raising a question whether cancellation is automatic or elective.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single definite election sentence with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the withholding instructions and the SSN/20% withholding note without tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the box A no-withholding election, which it limits rather than contradicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: As reproduced the representation is truncated mid-sentence ('no bankruptcy proceedings, attachment ... tax'), so the class of matters represented against cannot be fixed; even complete, a list ending in a general lien reference invites ejusdem generis argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the form addresses the owner's solvency or creditors, so there is no competing provision.
judgments.clause_name: 1) Representation as to bankruptcy, attachment, tax or lien

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause both ratifies unilateral 'corrections' noted under Home Office Endorsement and then says there can be no change in amount, age at issue, risk class, plan or benefits without the owner's written agreement, and the boundary between a ratifiable 'correction' and a prohibited 'change' is the ambiguous point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits directly against the Home Office Endorsement block (endorsed by attachment, effective December 1995) and against items 3, 4 and 6, which are themselves changes to amount, type and benefits, so the two could be read as pulling in opposite directions.
judgments.clause_name: 2) Ratification of corrections by Home Office Endorsement

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'If any part of the policy is cancelled by a change' releases the insurer from 'any claims or liability under such part', but 'part' and what counts as cancellation 'by a change' are undefined, and the premium-adjustment sentence is broken off.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with item 8 (cancel Supplementary Agreements), item 6's rider-termination parenthetical, and item 3's reduction of the basic amount, so the scope of the release relative to a mere reduction rather than cancellation is contestable.
judgments.clause_name: 3) Release on cancellation of part of policy
